name: ML Privacy & Model Security
description: Privacy attacks against ML (membership inference, model/data extraction, inversion) and federated-learning security.
narrative:
The earliest work in this collection treated ML privacy as a web and access-control problem rather than a property of the model itself. "Leaky Images: Targeted Privacy Attacks in the Web" (2019) showed how supposedly private shared images could be used to deanonymize specific users, while the following year the focus sharpened onto the models. "Exploring Connections Between Active Learning and Model Extraction" (2020) framed model stealing as a query-efficiency problem, and "Local Model Poisoning Attacks to Byzantine-Robust Federated Learning" (2020) opened the federated-learning threat front by showing that even "robust" aggregation could be subverted by malicious clients.

The early 2020s were dominated by federated learning, which became both the main attack surface and the main defense battleground. "FLAME: Taming Backdoors in Federated Learning" (2022) became the heavily cited reference point for backdoor defenses, while the attack literature broadened to inversion and membership inference against deployed models, as in "Are Your Sensitive Attributes Private? Novel Model Inversion Attribute Inference Attacks on Classification Models" (2022) and "Membership Inference Attacks and Defenses in Neural Network Pruning" (2022). At the same time researchers exposed weaknesses in the privacy-preserving variants of collaborative learning themselves, with "PCAT: Functionality and Data Stealing from Split Learning by Pseudo-Client Attack" (2023) and "VILLAIN: Backdoor Attacks Against Vertical Split Learning" (2023) showing that split and vertical learning leak too.

By 2024 the field matured toward consolidation and principled defense. Information-theoretic framing became a recurring theme across both extraction and inference, seen in "Inf2Guard: An Information-Theoretic Framework for Learning Privacy-Preserving Representations against Inference Attacks" (2024) and "ModelGuard: Information-Theoretic Defense Against Model Extraction Attacks" (2024), and the community began taking stock with systematization papers like "SoK: All You Need to Know About On-Device ML Model Extraction - The Gap Between Research and Practice" (2024).

The newest work has pivoted decisively toward large generative models and the lifecycle of data. Membership inference, the field's oldest privacy primitive, is now aimed at LLMs and multimodal systems in "Towards Label-Only Membership Inference Attack against Pre-trained Large Language Models" (2025) and "Membership Inference Attacks Against Vision-Language Models" (2025), and defenses such as "SOFT: Selective Data Obfuscation for Protecting LLM Fine-tuning against Membership Inference Attacks" (2025) target the fine-tuning stage specifically. Meanwhile the gradient-leakage thread that began with federated poisoning has been systematized in "SoK: Gradient Inversion Attacks in Federated Learning" (2025), and the agenda has expanded to machine unlearning and synthetic-data privacy, signaling that the area now spans the full data lifecycle from training to removal.

milestones.title: Leaky Images: Targeted Privacy Attacks in the Web
milestones.note: earliest listed work, framing ML-adjacent privacy as a web deanonymization problem before attacks moved into the models themselves

milestones.title: Local Model Poisoning Attacks to Byzantine-Robust Federated Learning
milestones.note: opened the federated-learning threat front by breaking aggregation rules thought to be robust

milestones.title: FLAME: Taming Backdoors in Federated Learning
milestones.note: became the dominant, most-cited reference point for defending federated learning against backdoors

milestones.title: PCAT: Functionality and Data Stealing from Split Learning by Pseudo-Client Attack
milestones.note: showed that privacy-preserving split learning itself leaks both functionality and training data

milestones.title: Inf2Guard: An Information-Theoretic Framework for Learning Privacy-Preserving Representations against Inference Attacks
milestones.note: marked the shift toward principled, information-theoretic defenses unifying multiple inference threats

milestones.title: Towards Label-Only Membership Inference Attack against Pre-trained Large Language Models
milestones.note: retargeted the field's oldest privacy primitive, membership inference, at pre-trained LLMs

milestones.title: SoK: Gradient Inversion Attacks in Federated Learning
milestones.note: systematized the gradient-leakage line of work, signaling the area's consolidation around data reconstruction
